verdict.rationale: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service is a managed Kubernetes service with kubectl access, so customers deploy their own workloads on bare-metal nodes, which implies running user-supplied container images. However, no evidence explicitly documents bringing a custom Docker image, a registry integration, or custom machine images. The docs also state customer clusters don't run VMs, which suggests there are no custom machine templates. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of deploying custom Docker/container images, private registry support, custom node/machine image or template support, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run my own Docker image or custom machine template with my exact environment

citations.quote: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) offers a managed Kubernetes service that lets you run clusters on bare metal servers in CoreWeave Cloud.
Create and download a `kubeconfig` for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like `kubectl`.
CKS runs Kubernetes directly on bare metal Nodes, without a hypervisor. Customer clusters don't run Virtual Machines.
